title: standby-router + adaptive-slo-thermostat: regional soft-eviction hotpatch
author: Evan Chen
release_notes: Backported standby routing for regional failover and added adaptive SLO thermostat to reduce oscillatory evictions under bursty KV pressure. Hotfix to be included in 2026.02.24 patch release.
description:
Motivation: In a recent incident (SUP-1291) we observed noisy evictions when a regional egress bottleneck caused aggressive tenant-level shedding. This PR introduces a standby-router that preserves inflight KV prefixes for tenants during regional reroutes, and an adaptive SLO thermostat that smooths eviction thresholds based on short-term KV pressure and latency quantiles. The goal is graceful degradation with fewer oscillations and faster recovery after transient egress spikes.

Changes in this PR (summary):
- New standby routing component: router/standby_router.go (coordination for transparent regional handoff, keeps per-tenant KV hold indices).
- Adaptive SLO thermostat: scheduler/thermostat.go (exponential cool-down + minimum hold window to prevent flapping).
- Telemetry hooks and backpressure marshal: telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go (adds histogram of KV pressure + tenant stay counts).
- Config knobs: configs/standby.yaml and defaults.yaml (tunable windows and memory caps).
- Integration test: tests/integration/regional_failover_standby_test.go (simulates bursty egress with tenant mixes).
- Minor docs: docs/operation/standby-router.md (operational runbook).

Commit summary: (3 commits, squashed on merge)
- 1) introduce standby router skeleton, initial tests, config schema
- 2) implement adaptive thermostat and integrate with serving runtime; add telemetry, add e2e toggles
- 3) fix race in KV hold map, add backpressure histogram labels, address lint failures

Files changed (high level):
- router/standby_router.go (+210 additions)
- scheduler/thermostat.go (+150 additions)
- telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go (+32 additions, +4 deletions)
- configs/standby.yaml (+10 additions)
- docs/operation/standby-router.md (+8 additions)
- tests/integration/regional_failover_standby_test.go (+20 additions)
- go.mod/go.sum (dep bumps for prometheus client)

Testing & CI notes:
- CI initially failed on unit tests in scheduler/thermostat.go due to a nondeterministic goroutine ordering; added a deterministic clock interface and re-ran.
- Lint complained about exported docstrings; fixed formatting in docs/operation/standby-router.md.
- Telemetry e2e asserts flaked in one run (timing dependent) so integration test was hardened to poll for histogram convergence instead of strict timing. Final CI result: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, lint).

Review conversation (high level):
- Priya Menon: "High-level: I like keeping standby state lightweight, but can we ensure per-tenant memory is bounded? Suggest adding per-tenant TTL + eviction priority. Also please add a small benchmark to confirm cost under normal traffic."
- Author (Evan): "Addressed: enforced per-tenant maxHoldBytes and default TTL=30s in configs/standby.yaml. Added microbenchmark router/bench/standby_bench_test.go (lightweight) and included results in the PR description."
- Sanjay Patel: "Concern about circuit interaction: thermostat changes thresholds; how does it play with our existing tenant-level circuit-breaker?"
- Author (Evan): "Thermostat exposes a `slo_inhibit` flag that temporarily raises threshold but consults the tenant circuit state before permitting any soft-eviction; added unit tests to validate the consult path. Kept behavior additive (no override of hard-circuit)."
- Karen O'Neill: "Telemetry labels are important — please ensure tenant id is redacted in metrics exported to external sinks."
- Author (Evan): "Telemetry now exports tenant cohort (hash bucket) rather than raw IDs; clarified in telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go and in docs. Added note to runbook about how to map cohorts for on-call context."
- Priya (after changes): "Approving pending one minor comment about constant naming style."

Risk assessment & rollout plan: "Low-to-moderate risk. Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_standby_router` (disabled by default). Thermostat enabled behind `adaptive_slo_thermostat` flag; thermostat defaults mimic previous static thresholds. Rollout plan: canary in one non-production region for 24h -> small production cohort (5% of traffic) for 6h -> 25% for 6h -> full rollout. Runbook includes emergency toggle to force immediate disable (console + API)."

Operational notes and metrics to watch (added to runbook):
- tenant_evictions_count (should decrease for transient bursts)
- kv_pressure_histogram (tail should compress, watch p95/p99)
- standby_hold_memory_bytes (per-region gauge; ensure below configured caps)
- thermostat_reopen_events (should show reduced reopen oscillations)

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs tuned eviction aggressiveness or added simple backoff. This PR is focused on short-lived state preservation during regional handoffs and an adaptive control loop (thermostat) that respects tenant hard-circuits and reduces oscillatory behavior while still providing SLO safeguards. The standby-router keeps only lightweight KV hold indices and uses cohorting + TTL to bound memory.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Priya and Sanjay and green CI. Changelog entry included and the hotfix scheduled in 2026.02.24 patch.

Notes for follow-ups (tracked as ENG tickets):
- ENG-4923: stronger memory accounting per-tenant and cross-region replica pruning
- ENG-4924: prometheus exporter scrubber for cohorts to support SAML-PII requirement
- ENG-4925: stress test harness for long-running standby_router with mixed tenant churn

Benchmarks (post-change micro-bench on c5-sim): "standby router overhead ~+2.1% CPU at 99th traffic case; eviction oscillation reduced by 48% in synthetic burst test compared to baseline."

If reverting: disable feature flags and deploy a rollback; standby state expires within TTL so rollback is soft.

End of PR description.
